events.criterion: TRUE on the date S.1717, or another bill that carries the operative text of S.1717 (a Medicare coverage pathway for FDA breakthrough-designated products), is signed into law or otherwise becomes law, as recorded on Congress.gov. readings: The forecaster tied passage to a shutdown compromise ('as part of the compromise'); enactment by any legislative vehicle counts, and the vehicle is not part of the event.

events.asset: December 2025 federal indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A.: conviction of Done Global
events.entity: US District Court hearing the December 2025 Done Global / Mindful Mental Wellness indictment (DOJ as prosecutor)
events.title: Done Global second federal indictment: conviction
events.proposition: Done Global, or an executive of Done Global charged in the December 2025 federal indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A., is convicted (jury verdict or accepted guilty plea) on that indictment.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a jury verdict of guilty, or of a guilty plea entered and accepted by the court, on any count of the December 2025 federal indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. (the indictment announced in the DOJ press release the post annotates), against Done Global as a corporate defendant or against any Done Global executive charged in that indictment. A superseding indictment in the same case is the same case. Convictions in the earlier Done case, convictions of co-defendants other than Done Global or its executives, deferred-prosecution or non-prosecution agreements, civil settlements and dismissals do not count. FALSE on the docket date of the disposition of the last count against the Done Global defendants without a conviction or plea, or at the deadline when no such conviction has been entered.

resolution_source.name: Federal court docket for the December 2025 Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. indictment (PACER via CourtListener); DOJ press releases as a secondary source

readings: 'This will go that far south' is read, from the DOJ boilerplate it reacts to (an indictment is only an allegation; defendants are presumed innocent), as the case ending with no defendant found guilty or pleading guilty.
'This' = the new (December 2025) indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A., not the earlier case in which the founders Ruthia He and David Brody were convicted.
A partial outcome (some defendants convicted, others acquitted or dismissed) is not 'that far south': the owen-1994 claim requires no conviction or guilty plea at all.
'Done' is read as Done Global, Inc. and the Done Global executives charged in the pending indictment.
'Convicted all over again' is read as a conviction on the indictment pending at the statement date, distinct from the earlier convictions the phrase refers back to.

owen-1994 (inverted) is on the same indictment; this event is TRUE on the first conviction of Done Global or a charged Done executive, which differs from the owen-1994 claim's FALSE trigger when a co-defendant other than Done is convicted.

related_timeline.event: DEA withdraws its proposed Schedule I placement of five tryptamines after hearing requests and says it will seek a new HHS scientific evaluation.

Ketamine Wellness Centers, a Delic Holdings subsidiary, abruptly shuts all of its ketamine clinics across nine states.
Field Trip Health & Wellness obtains CCAA creditor protection from the Ontario Superior Court; PwC named monitor and a sale process starts.
Second temporary extension of telemedicine flexibilities for controlled medications through December 31, 2024.
DEA stays the June 10, 2024 administrative hearing on Schedule I placement of DOI and DOC; the proposal remains pending.
Done Global CEO Ruthia He and clinical president David Brody are arrested on federal charges over an alleged $100M Adderall telehealth distribution scheme.
DEA publishes notice of an administrative hearing on the proposed marijuana rescheduling, initially set for December 2, 2024.
MHPAEA final rule published (released September 9): NQTL comparative-analysis and meaningful-benefit requirements, effective November 22, 2024, applicable plan years 2025 and 2026.
Compass delays COMP005 topline to Q2 2025 and COMP006 data to after the 26-week point (H2 2026) to protect blinding, and lays off 30% of staff.
Numinus agrees to sell its five Utah wellness clinics to Stella MSO and pivots to a data and technology model.
Third temporary extension of telemedicine flexibilities for controlled medications through December 31, 2025.

events.asset: ERISA fiduciary-breach litigation over employer group health plans that pleads mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations
events.entity: US federal district courts (complaint filed by plan participants, their counsel or the Department of Labor)
events.title: ERISA fiduciary lawsuit citing mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations is filed
events.proposition: A lawsuit is filed in a US federal court that pleads an ERISA breach-of-fiduciary-duty claim against the sponsor or fiduciaries of an employer group health plan and cites violations of the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act as a basis for the breach.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a complaint filed in a US federal district court within the window that (a) pleads a claim under ERISA for breach of fiduciary duty against the sponsor, plan committee or other named fiduciaries of an employer-sponsored group health plan over the plan's design or administration, whether brought by plan participants or by the Department of Labor, and (b) cites the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA, 'mental health parity') as a basis of the alleged breach, as shown by the complaint text. A suit only for denied benefits under ERISA section 502(a)(1)(B) against an insurer or administrator, a state-court suit, or an amended complaint in a case filed before the window does not count. Legal press reports are a finding aid only. FALSE when no such complaint has been filed by the deadline.
readings: 'ERISA lawsuit' is read, from the post's discussion of the Schlichter Bogard fiduciary-breach suits against employers (United Airlines, CHS, Universal Services of America, LabCorp), as a fiduciary-breach suit against a plan sponsor or its fiduciaries, not a benefit-denial suit against an insurer.
'The first' is read as 'at least one such suit is filed within the window'; the ledger does not verify that none existed before the statement date.
'Referencing mental health parity violations' = the complaint cites MHPAEA (or 'mental health parity') as a basis of the fiduciary breach.
